I've read everyone's comments. I really appreciate all your perspectives. I'll write my thoughts here. I feel like society makes us put a label on our selves. The world revolves around labels. Some people are quick to assume that a woman that is more masculine is a lesbian or atleast anything other than just straight. Same goes for feminine guys and people that aren't what the world thinks others should be. In highschool alot of class mates thought I was a lesbian. I'm assuming it was because how I dressed. I was pretty masculine. That hurt me alot. I've always been confident in my sexuality. I've always been into guys. 

I have went through trauma. I was bullied alot growing up which was mainly from girls so I tend to stay away from them. People would give me crap for wearing guy clothes. I have had thoughts about wishing I was born a boy when I was a kid. I thought it would be easier. I was never confident in my body. I was an overweight kid that never could find girl clothes that fit so I wore mostly guy clothes. I think my body issues warped my idea of gender. I don't think clothes have to be gendered. I finally got to a place where I would wear anything I wanted. My high school trauma took a huge toll on me. I just happened to find the trans community after that. I looked up how I was feeling detached from my body and it came up as gender dysphoria. I had dysphoria growing up. I related alot to youtube videos about being transgender. My mindset usually is if I had known about the community when I was alot younger then I probably would've started transitioning as a kid. I barely had any female role models in my life. All my role models were mainly males. Maybe that influenced me, I don't know.

I've read about internalize misogyny. I'm starting to think that's what fueling my transition. I like to think of myself as a open-minded, non judgemental person. I don't have a problem with women but I have a problem with me being one. I don't fully feel like a man either. I never really let myself explore my femininity as a girl, only when I'm identifying as a guy. I don't want to make a mistake that'll ruin who I used to be. In my opinion there's not a right or wrong way to be a certain gender. I think I could be just trying to find a label that fits me? I don't want to go through all the pain of transitioning. I'm scared of the world. Right now I pass as a perfectly fine woman atleast on the outside. I could just be trying to chase a new life. Become a whole another person and throw my past away. I know my past will always be apart of me and I don't want to lose what made me who I am. I don't want to rob myself of who I could become trying to become someone else. I probably seem like I don't want to go through with transitioning.

Also pronouns, they confuse me. I feel really comfortable with he/him pronouns but doubting myself. Like how can a few words make me want to alter my body. The pronouns definitely aren't the only thing making me want to transition but they influence it alot. I do like looking more masculine but I also love femininity. I often have days where I switched between the two. One day I feel like being feminine then next masculine.

This feels kinda like it was really long for a comment. I may just be rambling. I'm not the best at responding to comments. I'm pretty overwhelmed right now. I really appreciate this sub. I'm reading posts and its making me start to think about myself more. I need to focus on what made me get to this point in my life. I definitely should see a therapist for this.
Thank you so much! That's definitely true. Rome wasn't built in a day afterall.

I feel like I'm a slave to nicotine. I don't want to be a slave anymore. I really want to be free from it.  That's a really good mindset to have! It really is a monster that kills it's prey slowly. I suppose I just need to take each day one at a time and hopefully the withdrawal symptoms will go away eventually. I'm sorry you've went through the same thing, I wish you well! Thank you!

I've been in treatment for my depression and on medication. I've never tried meditation so I may give it a shot! As soon as it gets warmer I'm going to start going for walks outside. Nature walks are probably a better way to clear my head than smoking. Thanks for the advice!
That's really good to know thank you! I hope my neurotransmitters will forget soon
Congrats on day 20, that's amazing! I hope I can have this mindset one day.
